newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks close first 1997 session weaker.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks close first 1997 session weaker.

text.p: * Toronto stocks closed down 22.72 points, with decliners far outnumbering advancers. * Weak bonds and gold bullion caused early market decline but it partially recovered at day's end.
Toronto stocks ended their first trading day of the year on a weaker note on Thursday, taking their cue from a softer Canadian currency as well as weaker bonds and a low gold bullion price.
The TSE Composite 300 Index closed down 22.72 points at 5904.31, with 47.59 million shares worth C$876.48 million trading hands. Decliners outnumbered advancers 532 to 328 with 243 unchanged.
By mid-afternoon, the TSE 300 was down almost 55 points, but a sudden turnaround in the last half hour of trading gave the market back some of its strength, traders said.
"The boys decided it was time to put some cash back in the marketplace," said one trader. "The market just got too cheap."

Stocks were battered during the first half of the trading day after the gold price hit its lowest point in three years. Comex February gold ended down US$2.60 at $366.60 an ounce after falling to a life-of-contract low of $366.50.

The TSE's heavily weighted gold index fell 1.59 percent as a result, pulling down the overall TSE 300 index. Gold giant Barrick Gold Corp lost C$0.65 to close at C$38.60 while rival Placer Dome Inc closed down C$0.80 at C$29.25.

Weak bonds on both sides of the border also hurt equity trading, dealers said. Canadian and U.S. bonds fell after the December National Association of Purchasing Managers Index rose to 54.0 from 52.7 in November, surpassing expectations.
And many market players used the first official day of 1997 trading to lock in profits for tax reasons, traders said.
The market was still trading in thin, holiday volumes, which made dealing more volatile than usual, they said.
